# DS-06: Data Visualization and Storytelling (Tier 1)

**Subtrack:** Data Science  
**Unit scope:** Perceptual principles, honest encodings, uncertainty visualisation, narrative and audience-aware communication.

- **[DS-T1-015](DS-T1-015-the-truth-behind-the-chart/README.md): The Truth Behind the Chart: Forensics of Misleading Graphics.** Audit a gallery of published charts against an exact defect policy (truncated bars, dual axes, cherry-picked windows, area distortion, misleading colormaps, inverted axes, missing sources), compute Tufte's lie factor, and redraw each chart honestly as an inspectable matplotlib Figure.
- **[DS-T1-016](DS-T1-016-honest-about-uncertainty/README.md): Honest About Uncertainty: Interval Plots, Quantile Dotplots and Fan Charts.** Build a tested library that turns survey estimates and quantile forecasts into honest displays (Wilson interval plots, threshold-aligned quantile dotplots, nested fan charts), refuse incoherent forecasts, and write a one-page market bulletin for a maize-storage decision.
- **[DS-T1-017](DS-T1-017-hot-days-small-multiples/README.md): Hot Days, Six Cities: A Small-Multiples Climate Story from NASA POWER.** Parse real NASA POWER reanalysis data for six Nigerian cities, compute hot-day indicators under fixed and city-relative thresholds with explicit missing-data rules, and tell an honest small-multiples story about whether hot days are becoming more common.
